raw_text:
Great brief. Below is a 12-week, couch-to-5K plan tailored for a 24-year-old male with exercise-induced asthma (well-controlled on SABA), aiming to complete a 5K in 12 weeks. Emphasis is on gradual progression, proper warm-ups, warm-downs, asthma management, and recovery. Include optional cross-training and mobility work. Each week includes sessions, sets/reps or time, and guidance on intensity. Also provides nutrition and recovery notes. Adapt as needed for individual response.

Key considerations for asthma:
- Warm up with gradual intensity for at least 10 minutes; include dynamic movements and light jog.
- Use a SABA as prescribed 5–15 minutes before training if advised by clinician; carry inhaler during workouts.
- If symptoms (wheezing, coughing, chest tightness) occur, pause, use inhaler, resume when comfortable, or adjust intensity.
- Avoid abrupt sprinting in cold air; use a scarf/buff, warm air through a mask if necessary, and consider running indoors on cold days.
- Hydration and airway-healthy environment (avoid highly polluted or high-allergen days when possible).

Structure overview:
- 12 weekly plan, 3 days per week running (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat) with optional 1–2 cross-training or mobility days.
- Progressive run-walk intervals transitioning to continuous running by Week 9–12.
- Each week includes: Run days, Cross-training/strength days, Mobility/Recovery, plus optional accessibility notes for asthma.

Weeks 1–4: Build baseline aerobic capacity and technique
Goal: establish consistent habit, improve tolerance to longer continuous effort, and introduce run-walk strategy.

Week 1
- Tue (Session A): 20 minutes total
  - 5 min warm-up brisk walk
  - Run/walk: 1 min easy jog, 2 min walk x 6 cycles (total ~18 min), 2 min cool-down walk
  - 5 min gentle mobility (hip circles, ankle mobility)
- Thu (Session B): Strength & mobility (20–25 min)
  - Bodyweight circuit (2 rounds): 
    - Squats 12
    - Push-ups or incline push-ups 8–12
    - Glute bridges 12
    - Bird-dogs 10 per side
    - Plank 20–30 seconds
  - Mobility: hip flexor stretch, pectoral stretch, thoracic rotations
- Sat (Session C): Easy 25 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - 15–20 min easy jog (conversational pace)
  - 5 min cool-down walk
- Optional: 10–15 min light cross-training (cycling or swimming) on non-running days if energy allows.

Week 2
- Tue: 25 minutes total
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run/walk: 1 min jog, 3 min walk x 6 cycles (total ~24 min), 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (25–30 min)
  - Add 1 set to each exercise from Week 1
  - Include step-ups or lunges if tolerable
- Sat: 28 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - 3 cycles: jog 2 min, walk 2 min, jog 2 min
  - 5 min cool-down
- Focus: breathing technique, pace by conversational effort.

Week 3
- Tue: 28 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run/walk: 2 min jog, 2 min walk x 6 cycles (approx 28 min), 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (30 min)
  - Add backward lunges, rows with bands if available; 2–3 sets
  - Core: dead bug, side planks 15–20 seconds each side
- Sat: 30 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - 2 cycles: jog 4 min, walk 2 min
  - 4–5 min jog to finish, cool-down
- Injury/comfort check: ensure no niggles; asthma control unchanged.

Week 4
- Tue: 30 minutes total
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run/walk: 3 min jog, 2 min walk x 4 cycles (approx 28–30 min), 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (30–35 min)
  - Add controlled downhill walking if environment allows to build endurance without overload
- Sat: 32 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - 4 cycles: jog 3 min, walk 2 min
  - 5 min cool-down
- Focus: establish steady rhythm, monitor asthma symptoms closely.

Weeks 5–8: Increase running time, reduce walking, introduce steady-state effort
Goal: Move toward continuous running with longer stretches, still avoid high-intensity bursts.

Week 5
- Tue: 32 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 4 min, walk 2 min x 4 cycles (total ~28–32), 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (30–35 min)
  - Add light weights or resistance bands if available; total body emphasis
- Sat: 35 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 6 min, walk 2 min x 3 cycles
  - 5 min cool-down
- Cross-training: 20–30 min low-impact (cycling, swimming) on one non-running day if desired.

Week 6
- Tue: 34 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 6 min, walk 1–2 min x 4 cycles
  - 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (30–40 min)
  - Core and glute emphasis; include farmer’s carry if equipment available
- Sat: 38 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 8 min, walk 2 min x 2 cycles, then jog 6 min
  - 5 min cool-down

Week 7
- Tue: 36 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 9 min, walk 1–2 min x 2 cycles, jog 9 min
  - 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (35–40 min)
- Sat: 40 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: continuous 20–28 minutes if comfortable; otherwise, follow run/walk pattern: jog 5 min, walk 1 min x 4
  - 5 min cool-down

Week 8
- Tue: 38 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 10 min, walk 1–2 min x 2, jog 6–8 min
  - 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (40 min)
- Sat: 42 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 12–15 minutes continuous if tolerated; otherwise, extend run intervals gradually
  - 5 min cool-down
- Focus: reinforce tolerance to longer continuous segments.

Weeks 9–12: Build to 5K confidence, include a continuous run and taper toward race
Goal: Complete a continuous 5K by week 12; refine pacing, running economy, and recovery.

Week 9
- Tue: 40 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: jog 15 minutes continuous, walk 1–2 minutes, jog 10–15 minutes (total ~30–40 depending on comfort)
  - 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (40–45 min)
- Sat: 45 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: continuous 18–22 minutes at a comfortable pace; if tolerated, extend to 25–28 minutes
  - 5 min cool-down

Week 10
- Tue: 42 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: continuous 20–25 minutes; if needed, couple with short walk breaks to maintain rhythm
  - 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Strength & mobility (40–45 min)
- Sat: 50 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: continuous 28–32 minutes if comfortable
  - 5 min cool-down

Week 11
- Tue: 45 minutes
  - 5 min warm-up walk
  - Run: continuous 30 minutes at a light, conversational pace
  - 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Mobility, light strength (30–40 min)
- Sat: 40–50 minutes
  - Optional: Race-pace interval session
  - Example: 5 min warm-up, 6 × 2 minutes at a steady but challenging pace with 2 minutes easy between, 5 min cool-down

Week 12: Taper and race preparation
Goal: Fresh legs, confidence, readiness for 5K.

Week 12
- Tue: 30–35 minutes total
  - 5 min warm-up walk, 20–25 minutes easy continuous run, 5 min cool-down
- Thu: Mobility and light strength (25–30 min)
- Sat: 20–25 minutes easy jog with strides (4 × 20–30 seconds at near race pace, with full recovery)
- Optional: Short easy shake-out jog or walk on non-running days
- Race plan: 5K day pacing guidance (aim to start at a conservative pace, negative split if possible; plan for even splits or slightly negative).

General pacing and asthma management tips
- Aerobic intensity: Target conversational pace. If you are too winded to hold a basic conversation, slow down.
- Warm-up routine: 10–15 minutes progressive warm-up (dynamic movements, gradually increasing intensity), finishing with 2–3 minutes of light jog before the running interval.
- Cold-air days: Prefer indoor treadmill sessions or adjust to longer warm-ups, wear a scarf/buff over mouth/nose to warm inhaled air, and reduce intensity on the coldest days.
- Inhaler timing: If approved by GP, keep inhaler accessible and use as prescribed before workouts if needed; monitor for any adverse reactions.
- Hydration: Sip water consistently; avoid large gulps during workouts.

Strength and mobility guidance (during entire plan)
- Frequency: 2–3 strength sessions per week (non-consecutive days) with a focus on lower body, core, and shoulder girdle.
- Core exercises: dead bug, bird-dog, glute bridge march, side planks; aim for 2–3 sets of 10–15 reps or 20–30 seconds per side.
- Lower-body emphasis: squats, lunges, step-ups, glute bridges, single-leg RDL progressions as tolerance allows.
- Mobility: hip flexor, hamstring, calf, ankle dorsiflexion, thoracic spine mobility; include cooling down with 5–10 minutes of stretch.

Nutrition basics for training adaptation
- Protein: Target 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight per day to support recovery and muscle adaptation.
- Carbohydrates: Ensure adequate carbohydrate intake around workouts (1–3 hours pre-run; post-run within 1 hour with some protein and carbs).
- Hydration: Maintain baseline hydration; increase around workouts.
- Caloric intake: Maintain energy balance or mild surplus if aiming to gain performance.
- Micronutrients: Adequate iron, vitamin D, calcium, and magnesium are important; consider a multivitamin if dietary gaps exist.

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep: Aim for 7–9 hours per night.
- Recovery days: Prioritize light activity (walking, gentle cycling) and mobility work on off days.
- Signs to adjust: If asthma symptoms worsen (cough, chest tightness, wheeze), reduce intensity or duration and consult clinician if persistent.
- Injury management: If any joint pain or increased niggles appear, reduce load, add extra rest, and consider cross-training alternatives (swimming or cycling) to keep aerobic conditioning.

Optional customization notes
- If the client progresses faster, you can shorten the rest intervals earlier and replace some walk breaks with longer jogs, but maintain overall weekly load with progressive increases to run time.
- If the client struggles with fatigue, introduce one additional rest day between sessions or revert to run/walk cycles from earlier weeks and progress with smaller increments.

Checklist for the trainer
- Check asthma status and ensure inhaler plan is clearly documented for the client.
- Confirm hydration, proper warm-up, and cool-down protocols are followed in each session.
- Track weekly progress: total running time, distance (if possible), and perceived exertion.
- Adjust plan based on response: if symptoms occur, scale back the progression by 20-30% and repeat the preceding week’s structure before proceeding.

This 12-week plan should guide a safe and progressive transition from couch to 5K, with emphasis on asthma management, gradual progression, and consistent recovery. If you want, I can tailor the plan to the client’s current weekly schedule (days available, preferred training time, equipment).
